'''Henry Roy Brahana''' (16 August 1895 in [[Lowell, Vermont]] – 15 October 1972 in [[Dennis, Massachusetts]]) was a mathematician, specializing in [[metabelian group]]s and related geometric structures.

H. Roy Brahana received his PhD from [[Princeton University]] in 1920 under the direction of [[Oswald Veblen]]. In the autumn of 1920,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Notes and News|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=27|date=May 1920|page= 237|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gdZNAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA237|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1921-03418-5|doi-access=free}}</ref> he joined the mathematics department of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] and remained there until his retirement in 1963. Brahana was the editor for the publication by the [[University of Illinois Press]] of the collected works of [[George Abram Miller]] in 5 volumes, coming out in the years 1935, 1939, 1946, 1955, and 1959. The H. Roy Brahana Prize for undergraduates at U. of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign was established in his honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.uiuc.edu/UndergraduateProgram/awards/brahana.html|title=The H. Roy Brahana Prize, Department of Mathematics, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|website=uiuc.edu}}</ref> His doctoral students include [[Robert M. Thrall]].

==Selected publications==
*"Systems of circuits on two-dimensional manifolds." Annals of Mathematics (1921): 144–168. {{doi|10.2307/1968030}}
*"Regular maps on an anchor ring." American Journal of Mathematics 48, no. 4 (1926): 225–240. {{doi|10.2307/2370598}}
*"Regular maps and their groups." American Journal of Mathematics 49, no. 2 (1927): 268–284. {{doi|10.2307/2370756}}
